items.response:
Sorry about the heel, a sore first step in the morning after a long run is worth getting looked at. I'll look for physio openings next week after work or on Saturday. I don't have a clinic saved for you, so I'll check availability and ask before booking.
Action: Search physio clinics near you for after-work and Saturday slots next week, then send you the best two or three options to pick from.

That's a rotten way to lose a Saturday evening with Leo, and one message from your boss pulling you into Looker is exactly what makes it feel worse. The dip can wait until Monday, and nothing about it needs to be solved tonight. Want help getting your head out of it?
Action: I'll draft a short, calm reply to Tom for you to send (or hold until Monday): 'Saw this, I'll dig into Thursday's dip first thing Monday and send you what I find.' Then I'll leave the dashboards alone until Monday morning.

I'm so sorry, four years tomorrow for your dad, Vikram. Of course, let's make the day gentle so you have room for the diya in the evening. I'll look at tomorrow and see what can move, shrink or be declined, and I won't change anything until you've seen it.
Action: Pull up tomorrow's calendar and send you a proposed lighter version (what to keep, what to move, what to decline), with the evening kept completely clear.

Beagles like Biscuit were bred to sing out when they hear something, and a siren sounds just like a very big dog howling, so he joins in to say 'I hear you!' It's his way of talking back, not because he's scared or upset. For Ellie: 'Biscuit thinks the fire truck is a giant dog calling to him, so he answers with his loudest song.'
Action: Offer to shorten it or add a fun fact for her age if you tell me how old Ellie is.

That makes sense, it's easy to spiral when a call goes unanswered and you feel guilty about skipping the weekend one. A dead phone battery is the most likely explanation, but let's still check rather than leave it hanging. I'll look through your messages for anything from her.
Action: Check your texts and WhatsApp for anything from your mom, and if there's nothing, set a reminder for you to try calling again at a time you choose today.

That sounds like the right kind of Saturday. Nothing needs you, so I'll hold the non-urgent stuff until Monday.
Action: Stay quiet and keep everything parked, including the drop-off research, until you ask for it.

I don't have that episode summary in front of me, so I won't guess at the title. I'll search for the summary and pull the episode's name and link so you can send it to Aisha.
Action: Search our past summaries and notes for the developer-platform pricing episode, then send you the title and link.

Here's a draft for Hannah: 'Hi Hannah, thank you so much for taking Biscuit out tomorrow morning! We're leaving at 5 and the cottage doesn't allow dogs. Heads up: if a fire truck or any siren goes by he'll howl at it, it's harmless, he just loves joining in. Text me anything you need!' As for why: beagles were bred to sing out, and a siren sounds like another dog howling, so he answers it.
Action: I'm missing the details Hannah needs (what time to come by, how you'll get her in, food and walk routine), so I'll ask you for those before sending.

Sending the text to Rui now. For next Saturday the 14th, I'll look for somewhere walkable from home in Leslieville or Riverside that takes a table for four. I don't know what time you want or whether anyone has dietary needs, so I'll check with you before booking.
Action: Send the message to Rui, then shortlist 3 restaurants for 4 on Sat 14th and ask you the preferred time and any dietary needs before I reserve.

A dinosaur it is. I'll look for a size 7 dinosaur costume under $50 that will arrive in time for Friday 30 Jan, since delivery time matters more than the exact style.
Action: Search for size 7 dinosaur costumes under $50 with delivery before Fri 30 Jan, order the best-reviewed one, and send you the confirmation and arrival date.

Easy. I'll put together a simple basket of after-school snacks for three kids and set pickup for 3:00 tomorrow. I don't know about any allergies or dislikes for Jun and his sister, so I'll check that quickly before placing it.
Action: Build the PC Express cart (fruit, crackers, cheese, something sweet and a drink) for pickup at 3:00 tomorrow, and ask you about any allergies before checkout.

I'll let Marcus know you're thinking about it. Here's a draft for the note: 'Dear Grace and Daniel, Thank you for such a warm Christmas in Ottawa, from the 24th to the 28th. We loved every minute, and the leftovers you sent home with us fed us well into the new year. With love, Riya, Sam and Leo.'
Action: Reply to Marcus that you'll think about it, and adjust the note's wording if you'd like it warmer or shorter.

I don't have the price in front of me yet, so I'd rather check than guess. Once I open the Kanchi Silks link I can see the price and compare it with similar sarees from other sellers, which will tell us whether it's fair.
Action: Open the saved Kanchi Silks link, read the price, and compare it with comparable sarees (fabric, zari work, weave) before telling you whether it looks reasonable.

I love that idea. I don't have the story of how you two met saved, and the best callback depends on the details. A few starters: recreate the food, drinks or music from back then, write each other short letters about your first impressions and swap them over dessert, or build a little photo slideshow.
Action: Ask you to tell me how you met so I can turn one of these into a proper plan with a shopping list.

Partly. Written Portuguese is quite readable if you know Spanish, but spoken Portuguese is much harder to follow, because the sounds and rhythm are very different. You'll get by, especially for reading signs and menus, and slowing down and asking people to repeat will help.
Action: Make you a short list of key Portuguese phrases for the Lisbon trip, where the words differ most from Spanish, and save it to your notes.

A paleontologist AND a pizza chef, and 'obviously' on the same day. That's a very Leo plan, and Sam's question was perfectly fair.
Action: Add this to a running note of Leo's funny lines so you have it later, and I'll start it if one doesn't exist.

Here's one: 'Happy birthday, Tom! Thanks for being great to work with, hope today is a good one. Riya'. If you want it a touch warmer: 'Happy birthday, Tom, glad to be on your team. Enjoy the day!'
Action: Pick the one you like and I'll polish it, so you can sign the card tonight.

Since you love Tana French, I'd start with one of hers in hardcover, 'The Hunter' for example, as it works well for a fellow mystery reader (worth checking that Priya hasn't read it). Card idea: 'Priya, a slow-burn mystery for a good weekend. So glad you're coming. Love, Riya.'
Action: Check which local bookstores have a hardcover copy in stock and for how much, then send you the options and the card to approve before I order.

I don't have a record of you picking them up, so I won't guess. I'll check your receipts and order confirmations since before Christmas, and your to-do list, to see if they were bought.
Action: Search your email and receipts for a furnace filter purchase, then tell you whether it was done and what size, or that I found nothing.

I'd use one shared database in Notion that anyone can add to, with a weekly triage view. Suggested fields: date, merchant, source (support, sales call, reply to your updates), summary, verbatim quote, category (bug, UX, feature request, pricing), severity, status, owner and linked Linear ticket. Add a short intake form so people don't have to find the right place.
Action: Create the draft database with those fields and a 'To triage this week' view, then share it with you before it goes to the team.

I don't have the results of that search saved, and I don't want to invent train times. I'll look for it in our history from that day.
Action: Search our past chats and notes for 27 Feb, and if I can't find it, re-run the VIA Rail search for Friday evenings Toronto to Ottawa and tell you the schedule may differ from what we saw.

Happy to. Which dates should I give her? I'd rather not guess and have her block the wrong days. Here's the text I'll send once I have them: 'Hi Hannah, you kindly offered to help with Biscuit a while back. Would you be able to feed and walk him while we're away from [dates]? We'll pay you, of course. No worries at all if it doesn't work.'
Action: Wait for the travel dates, then send the text to Hannah.

Here's a draft: 'Reminder: the beta retro is Thursday at 2pm in Room 4B. Please add your sticky notes to the Miro board before then so we can spend the time on discussion. Thanks, all!'
Action: Keep it as a draft for you to approve, then post it in #payouts-launch when you say go.

On it. I'll pull the open risks for the payouts launch from Linear and group them by workstream in one Notion doc, with owner, status and next step for each, so it's ready for standup tomorrow.
Action: Query Linear for open payouts launch risks, build the Notion doc, and send you the link.

Nice thought. I'll send a coffee and a snack to Riverdale for around 3:30, to room 214. I don't know Sam's usual order, so I'll keep it simple.
Action: Place a delivery of a coffee and a snack to room 214 at Riverdale for 3:30, and ask you for his usual order first if you'd like it exact.

I don't have either of those in front of me, and I won't guess at times or counts. I'll look at Tom's calendar for that February day and the log of the May sync with Sam's school calendar.
Action: Check Tom's calendar for the open slots that day and the May sync log for how many school events came across, then report back with the exact numbers.

Happy long weekend! Here's a sensible order:
1. Find the extension cord (you may need it for the rest)
2. Fix Leo's bike chain
3. Hang the hallway mirror
4. Sort the garage recycling
5. Plant the tomato seedlings (late afternoon, before it gets dark)
Action: Save this as a checklist in your notes so you can tick things off today.

I'll pull what we have on Instant Payouts beyond the beta merchants (open payouts tickets and launch risks in Linear, plus the readiness status) and draft a reply to Olivia. I won't give her a date that isn't confirmed, since it's going to a prospect.
Action: Pull open payouts tickets and launch risks from Linear grouped by workstream, draft the Slack reply to Olivia, and show it to you before sending.

Fun. I'll look for pumpkin patches within 45 minutes that are open this afternoon and not too crowded, since you're leaving around 1:30. I won't name one from memory without checking hours first.
Action: Search for pumpkin patches within a 45-minute drive, check today's opening hours and reviews for crowds, and send you the best two or three options.

Good call from Carlos. I'll look for an upper-intermediate grammar book with a strong subjunctive section, plenty of exercises and a full answer key. I'm assuming this is for Spanish.
Action: Find the top two or three options with the answer key included, compare price and delivery, and order the best fit, then confirm what I picked and when it arrives.

Sounds good. Since you said to just book what's best, I'll find a hotel in or near the Plateau for Fri 6 to Sun 8 Feb under $250 a night, with good reviews and free cancellation if possible.
Action: Search Plateau hotels, book the best-rated one under $250 a night for those two nights, and send you the confirmation.

Happy to help. I don't have his birthday or your anniversary dates handy in this chat, so I'll check them first. For gift ideas I'd want to know what he's been into lately, but a nice default is an experience you do together.
Action: Ask you for both dates and two or three things he's been into lately, then suggest gifts and a celebration plan, and set a reminder three weeks ahead of the anniversary so it's not a last-week scramble.

Great, Leo's turning 8. I'll check whether Wonder Workshop does parties for twelve kids on Saturday 23 Jan 2027 and what the packages cost, rather than guessing at numbers.
Action: Look up Wonder Workshop's party packages, group size limits, pricing and deposit for Sat 23 Jan 2027, and contact them if the site doesn't say, then report back.

Here's a first pass for the week back, before it gets properly cold:
- Thursday morning: be home 8:00-10:00 for the cabinet delivery
- Check and replace the furnace filter
- Disconnect outdoor hoses and shut off exterior taps
- Clear eavestroughs and check for drafty windows and doors
Action: Turn this into a checklist spread across the week, with the Thursday cabinet delivery blocked on your calendar.

I don't see anything from Nate yet, but let me check your texts and email properly. Remember he prefers texts, so I won't call him.
Action: Check your messages and email for a text from Nate since his Barzotti call, and if nothing is there, text him (no calls) to ask for the schedule update.

Here's a kid-friendly answer: poppies grew on the battlefields of World War I in Belgium and France. A Canadian doctor, John McCrae, wrote the poem 'In Flanders Fields' in 1915 about them, and the poppy became a symbol to remember the soldiers who died. We wear one to say thank you and that we haven't forgotten.
Action: Offer to shorten it into two sentences for Leo or find a short, age-appropriate video if he wants more.

A board-gamey do-over sounds perfect. I'll keep it to a Saturday, so Sunday marking isn't in the way. I'd look at board game cafes, or a game night at home with takeout if you'd rather.
Action: Check both your calendars for open Saturdays, search board game cafes nearby, and send you a couple of options with dates to choose from before I book anything.

Adding that action item with you as owner. For Prince Edward County, six stops on Saturday is a lot, so I'd check drive times and opening hours before committing, and probably move one or two things to Sunday.
Action: Add the action item to the recap, then draft a Saturday itinerary leaving at 8 with drive times and hours, flagging anything that doesn't fit.

Glad the haiku landed. Poet in residence it is.
Action: Nothing needed, but I'm happy to do a Friday one if the title sticks.

Good questions. From what I can see, the only fixed charge I have in front of me is home internet, Bell Fibe at $95 a month, but I don't want to guess at the rest. I'll check the batteries order and put together the history.
Action: Pull the recurring charges from your TD and Visa statements, check the Amazon batteries order status in your email, and summarize what you've used me for so far.

For Tom, I'd block any full OOO days plus half-days for early leaves in December. I don't know your plans yet, so I'll check the calendar and school dates first. For Leo's 'that thing' from last winter, I don't have it saved, so I'll go looking.
Action: Pull your December calendar and school holiday dates, list candidate days to block, and search our past chats and notes for what you did when school was shut so Leo can have his 'thing' again.

I haven't read it yet, so I can't say whether it's worth it. I'll go through Carlos's email and compare it with what you're doing now in terms of cost, time and what you'd get out of it.
Action: Open Carlos's email, summarize the offer, check your calendar for conflicts, and give you a recommendation on worth it or overkill.

Sure. I'll put a 15-item spring cleaning checklist in your notes and look for options to haul the old couch from the basement. Bulky item pickup and private haulers both exist, but I'll check current pricing before suggesting one.
Action: Create the checklist note and get quotes or booking options for couch removal from the basement, then send you the choices.

Sorry about Sam's migraine. For an unscented gift, good bets are local food (maple syrup or baked goods), a nice book, or a handmade bowl or mug. Skip anything with fragrance like soap, candles or flowers.
Action: Search for shops in Ottawa open tomorrow morning with those options and send you two or three ideas for Grace and Daniel to pick from.

Sunday scaries are the worst, and an extra hour of clock doesn't fix them. Let's make tomorrow smaller: I'll pick the few things that actually need you and leave the rest. One thing is waiting for you, which slot to send for the payout edge cases meeting with Aisha and Diego.
Action: Put the laptop away tonight, and in the morning I'll send you a short list of your top three things for tomorrow plus the meeting slot to confirm.
